name: movements-093
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: Trap press. Equipment: Barbell + Bench + Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Laying flat with arm pointing straight upwards, elbow fully extended, use only your shoulder to raise the weight as high as comfortable and back to rest.

Row 1 column 2: Trap-3 Raise. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: 1. Hinge forwards and bend your knees slightly. Depress and retract the shoulder you will use. Rest the other hand on your knee. 2. Raise your hand about 15 degrees overhead, maintaining the position of your shoulder.

Row 1 column 3: Treadmill Cardio. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: It's a cardiovascular workout performed on a treadmill to improve endurance, burn calories, and promote heart health. It offers multiple benefits, such as the ability to easily adjust speed and incline, allowing for a variety of workouts, from hill walking to high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and tempo runs. To optimize results, it's important to vary your workouts. Benefits of Treadmill Cardio: - Improved Cardiovascular Health: Regular aerobic exercise on a treadmill strengthens the heart and lungs, which can help prevent heart disease. - Weight Loss: By burning calories, treadmill training can be an effective tool for weight loss and maintaining a healthy weight. - Muscle Strengthening: It strengthens the muscles in the legs and glutes, helping to prevent muscle loss, which is especially important with age. - Training Flexibility: Allows you to vary speed, incline, and intervals, making your workout more dynamic and adaptable to different fitness levels. Types of Treadmill Training: - Hill Walking: Increasing the incline of the treadmill and walking at a brisk pace can improve endurance and work your leg muscles. - Endurance Jog: A run at a comfortable, steady pace that keeps your heart rate in a target zone (such as Zone 2) to build endurance. - Interval Training: Alternating periods of high intensity (fast running) with periods of low intensity (easy walking or jogging) to maximize calorie burn and cardiovascular improvement. - Tempo Run: A run at a steady, sustained pace that is slightly faster than a normal jog, which challenges your ability to sustain a more intense effort for an extended period.

Row 1 column 4: Tricep Side Stretch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Bring right arm across your body and over your left shoulder, holding your elbow with your left hand, until you feel a stretch in your tricep. Then repeat for your other arm.

Row 2 column 1: Assisted machine triceps dip. Equipment: Assisted dip / chin station. Exercise guide: Choose sufficient assistance and hold the dip handles securely. Place your knees or feet on the platform according to the machine's setup. With shoulders controlled, bend your elbows to lower through a comfortable range, keeping them near your sides. Press the handles down to extend your arms without jerking or shrugging. Control the platform throughout and step off carefully.

Row 2 column 2: Triceps Overhead (Dumbbell). Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: * Ellbogen fixieren * Muskulatur anspannen * Kein Schwung holen * Kontrollierte Bewegung * Langsame Bewegung * Immer angewinkelt lassen * Nicht überdehnen

Row 2 column 3: Triceps push up. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Push ups for targeting triceps. - Start with a plank position with your hands directly below your shoulders, feet together. - When descending, keep your elbows pinned to your sides. Upper arms straight back. - Lower until your chest touches the floor, then return.

Row 2 column 4: Triceps Stretch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Reach your hand behind your head, grasp your elbow and gently pull. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.

Row 3 column 1: TRX dips. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Start with the hands on the suspension trainer and feet on the ground. Your hands should be under your shoulders with the feet slightly in front. Lower yourself by bringing the hips between the handles and flexing the elbows. Extend the elbows to come back to the starting position and repeat.

Row 3 column 2: TRX gorilla biceps curl. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: We'll stand facing the TRX straps and grab them with our fists facing each other, facing forward, with our arms fully extended at about shoulder-width apart. We'll keep our body straight, backward, as in the previous exercises, since we'll be lifting our body toward the TRX straps by activating our biceps. Our body will be straight, with our feet flat on the floor. This time, we'll place our arms open to the sides and at chest height. The movement we'll perform is a contraction toward our chest. To achieve this, we'll bend our elbows so that, by activating our biceps, we can pull our body toward the straps.

Row 3 column 3: TRX hammer curl. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Place the grips as if they were a continuation of the straps. We will position our arms stretched forward and our body leaning back, completely straight. The biceps muscles will activate as you bend your elbows to bring your body towards the straps. The contraction movement will end with a slight outward movement of the hands, due to the grip we are using.

Row 3 column 4: TRX Obliques. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: 1. Place your feet in the stirrups and assume a high plank with your hands directly beneath your shoulders. 2. Pull your knees to your right elbow, then push them back out and to the centre.
